body.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), suppose \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) is fixed, the primitive conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\) hold along the base law and contiguous joint-chart paths, and \(\sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1)\). Then \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},\] \(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and \(P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\). The contiguous-path expansion makes the estimator regular and efficient for the observed joint-bridge functional.
body.justification: The mixed-bias and cross-fit reductions identify the correct high-level route.
body.gap: The learned efficient-signal convergence and its contiguous-path uniformity are not proved.
body.consumer: Wald reporting remains conditional rather than certified under the current primitive list.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the efficient asymptotic linear expansion and its locally uniform contiguous-path version for the explicit estimator from primitive rates.
obligation.obstruction: The theorem depends on the unresolved general canonical-gradient result and the unresolved learned-projection lemma. Its phrase that primitive conditions hold along contiguous paths does not itself provide a uniform triangular-array projection expansion.
obligation.attempted: The foldwise drift was bounded by the exact mixed-bias identity using either the primal residual times the treatment error or the adjoint residual times the outcome error. Conditional holdout variance yields the empirical-process reduction once learned-signal convergence is supplied, but that premise is not yet derived.
obligation.partial_result:
If \(\|\widehat\psi-\theta-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2=o_p(1)\) foldwise and the weighted mixed bias is \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\), then cross-fitting gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).
\]
For \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}<\infty\), the i.i.d. central limit argument and truncation-based laws of large numbers then give pointwise asymptotic normality, variance consistency, and Wald coverage.  The missing primitive learned-projection bound and its locally uniform contiguous-path version prevent the advertised theorem from being closed.
